what_its_for: This eye drop or eye ointment is used to treat eye infections and inflammation at the same time. It contains two medicines: tobramycin (an antibiotic that fights bacteria) and dexamethasone (a steroid that reduces swelling, redness, and irritation). Your doctor may prescribe it after eye surgery or for certain bacterial eye infections that also cause inflammation.
how_to_take: Wash your hands thoroughly before and after using this medicine. For eye drops: Tilt your head back, pull down your lower eyelid to form a small pocket, and place the prescribed number of drops into the pocket. Close your eye gently for 1 to 2 minutes and press lightly on the inner corner of your eye (near your nose) to help keep the medicine in your eye. Do not let the dropper tip touch your eye, eyelid, or any surface to avoid contamination. For eye ointment: Pull down your lower eyelid and squeeze a small ribbon of ointment (about half an inch) into the pocket. Close your eye and roll it gently to spread the medicine. Your vision may be blurry for a few minutes after using the ointment — this is normal. If you wear contact lenses, remove them before using this medicine and wait at least 15 minutes before putting them back in.
dosing: For the suspension (eye drops): The usual dose is 1 to 2 drops into the affected eye(s) every 4 to 6 hours. During the first 24 to 48 hours, your doctor may tell you to use it more often, such as every 2 hours. For the ointment: Apply a small amount to the affected eye(s) 3 to 4 times a day, or as directed. Always follow the exact dosing instructions your doctor or pharmacist gives you. Do not use more or less than prescribed.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do not double up or apply extra doses to make up for the one you missed.
storage: Store the eye drops and ointment at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep the bottle or tube tightly closed when not in use. Do not freeze. Keep out of reach of children. Shake the eye drop suspension well before each use. Throw away any unused medicine after you finish your prescribed course of treatment, or after the expiration date on the label.
what_to_avoid: Do not touch the dropper or tube tip to your eye, fingers, or any other surface, as this can introduce germs into the medicine. Avoid wearing contact lenses while you have an active eye infection unless your doctor says it is okay. Do not drive or operate machinery right away if your vision is blurry after applying the medicine — wait until your vision clears. Do not use this medicine for longer than prescribed, as overuse of the steroid component can raise pressure inside the eye and may lead to other eye problems. Do not share this medicine with anyone else.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience: increased eye pain, redness, or swelling that gets worse instead of better; vision changes or sudden vision loss; seeing halos around lights; eye discharge that increases or changes; signs of an allergic reaction such as severe itching, rash, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing; or if your symptoms do not improve within a few days of starting treatment. Also tell your doctor if you have a history of glaucoma or cataracts, as this medicine can sometimes raise eye pressure or worsen those conditions.
when_it_works: You may start to notice some improvement in redness and irritation within the first 1 to 2 days of treatment. The infection and inflammation should continue to improve over the next several days. It is very important to finish the full course of treatment your doctor prescribed, even if your eye feels better, to make sure the infection is completely cleared.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Use this medicine only if your doctor decides the benefit outweighs the risk. Children: This medicine can be used in children, but only under the close supervision of a doctor. Elderly patients: No special dose adjustments are typically needed, but older adults should still follow all instructions carefully. Patients with glaucoma or a history of high eye pressure: Use with caution and attend all follow-up appointments, as steroid eye drops can raise eye pressure over time.
